{{short description|American mathematician}}
[[File:Betsy Stovall Oberwolfach 2017.jpg|thumb|Stovall at [[Mathematisches Forschungsinstitut Oberwolfach|Oberwolfach]] in 2017]]
'''Lindsay Elizabeth "Betsy" Stovall''' is an American mathematician known for her research in [[harmonic analysis]]. She is the Mary Herman Rubinstein Professor in the College of Letters & Science at the [[University of Wisconsin–Madison]].

==Education and career==
Stovall is a graduate of [[Emory University]],<ref name=new>{{cite web|url=https://ls.wisc.edu/news/new-faculty-qa-betsy-stovall-mathematics|title=New faculty Q&A: Betsy Stovall (Mathematics)|publisher=University of Wisconsin–Madison College of Letters & Science|access-date=2022-01-06}}</ref> and received her PhD in 2009 from [[University of California, Berkeley]], where her advisor was [[F. Michael Christ]].<ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=153888}}</ref> Before joining the University of Wisconsin in 2012, she was associate adjunct professor at the [[University of California, Los Angeles]].<ref name=new/>

She is the Associate Secretary for the Central Section of the [[American Mathematical Society]], with a term beginning in February 2022.<ref>{{cite web |title=Michelle Manes and Betsy Stovall named AMS Associate Secretaries |url=https://www.ams.org/news?news_id=6913 |publisher=American Mathematical Society |access-date=5 January 2022}}</ref>

Stovall was a member of the [[American Mathematical Society]] (AMS) Abstracts Editorial Committee from 2022 - 2023.<ref>{{Cite web |title=AMS Committees |url=http://www.ams.org/about-us/governance/committees/abstracts-past.html |access-date=2023-03-29 |website=American Mathematical Society |language=en}}</ref>

==Recognition==
Stovall was named to the 2023 class of Fellows of the [[American Mathematical Society]], "for contributions to harmonic analysis".<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ams.org/cgi-bin/fellows/fellows_by_year.cgi|title=2023 Class of Fellows|publisher=American Mathematical Society|access-date=2022-11-09|archive-date=2022-11-09|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221109214706/https://www.ams.org/cgi-bin/fellows/fellows_by_year.cgi|url-status=dead}}</ref> In 2026, she received the [[AWM Service Award]] "for spearheading the local organizing efforts to create a spectacular 2025 AWM Research Symposium in Madison."<ref>{{Cite web |title=AWM Service Award 2025 |url=https://awm-math.org/awards/awm-service-award/awm-service-award-2025/ |access-date=2026-04-10 |website=Association for Women in Mathematics (AWM) |language=en-US}}</ref>
